summary: Fix temporal anchoring (identity-91 root, aspectual verbs, past-time adverbs, result-now depends-on, have-degree-91 exception), superlative ARG2/ARG5 and 上 postposition, Chinese PropBank role numbering, attributes on identity-91/have-degree-91, shared-subject re-entrancy, fused negation, narrowed already+stop rule, nested and-pairs, coref checklist.

edits.old: - past-time adverbs (*once, formerly*; 曾, 曾经) are `:temporal`;
edits.new: - past-time adverbs (*once, formerly*; 曾, 曾经) are `:temporal` (in the graph only; they get no temporal triple, see 5.1);

edits.old: - a locative postposition after a time noun (X 时, X 中, X 以来) is a `:temporal` node with the time noun as `:op1`.
edits.new: - a locative postposition after a time or period noun (X 时, X 中, X 以来, X 上 as in *in the history of ...*) is a `:temporal` node for the postposition with the noun as `:op1`, attached to the word it scopes over (often the head noun).

edits.old: Do not use `:degree` on a property verb for a superlative; use `have-degree-91`.
edits.new:
Do not use `:degree` on a property verb for a superlative; use `have-degree-91`. Its `:ARG2` is the property word itself. If the property is a verb with its own object (*rich in X, full of X*, 富X, 充满X), keep that verb as an event with its object (`(r / V-01 :ARG1 X :aspect state)`) and put it under `:ARG2`; do not drop the verb or put the object noun there. Use `:ARG5` only for an explicit comparison set (*among N, of all N*, 在…中); a scope like *in history* is a `:temporal` postposition node (2.1), not `:ARG5`.

**Chinese role numbering.** For every Chinese predicate, look up its Chinese PropBank frames. Choose the sense whose role descriptions fit (the belonging/membership sense of a verb is often not -01), and use exactly the numbered roles that roleset defines. Many Chinese intransitive and change-of-state verbs have only `:ARG0` (the thing that ceases, changes or acts). Do not default the theme to `:ARG1` by English habit.

edits.old: - **Unexpressed participants.** Do not fill a roleset slot with a participant the text does not express. Re-enter a node only when the text itself expresses that participant in that role.
edits.new: - **Unexpressed participants.** Do not fill a roleset slot with a participant the text does not express. Re-enter a node only when the text itself expresses that participant in that role. A subject shared through a control, serial or purpose/means frame (以 X 而 Y, *known for doing X*, *try to X*) counts as expressed: re-enter it as the subject of the embedded verb too.

edits.old: A true idiom stays one concept.
edits.new: A true idiom stays one concept. When such a parallel-noun pair is one item of a longer list, nest it as its own `and` inside the outer `and`.

edits.old: - **already + stop/cease** (已经停止…) describing the current situation is `state`.
edits.new:
- **already + an aspectual stop verb governing another event** (已经停止 doing X) describing the current situation is `state`. A lexical termination verb with no governed event (a publication ceased, an organization dissolved) is `performance`, even with 已经.
- **Abstract predicates:** `identity-91` gets `:aspect state`; `have-degree-91` gets no `:aspect` (the event under its `:ARG2` does).

edits.old:
- Negation: `:polarity -` on the negated concept (没, 不, 未, *not, never*); the event's modal strength is
  then negative (5.2).
edits.new:
- Negation: `:polarity -` on the negated concept (没, 不, 未, *not, never*); the event's modal strength is
  then negative (5.2). Exception: when the negation is fused into one verb word (未经 type), write no `:polarity -`; mark only `full-negative` at the document level.

edits.old: - Every event node must get exactly one temporal parent. The only exception is a pure copular identity state (`identity-91`), which is left out of the temporal structure; it still gets its modal parent.
edits.new:
- Past-time adverbs (*once, formerly*, 曾, 曾经) are not reference times: give them no triple and link their event directly, `(document-creation-time :before e)`.
- A completed event whose result describes the present situation (a status reached, a name or evaluation given: a naming/evaluation passive, 已经 + a completed change) is linked as `(document-creation-time :depends-on e)`.
- An aspectual verb (*stop, begin, continue*) and the event it governs are `:overlap`, never `:before`/`:after`.
- Every event node must get exactly one temporal parent. Two exceptions:
  - `identity-91` is left out of the temporal structure but still gets its modal parent. When a sentence's root is `identity-91`, choose as anchor the event inside the predicate noun that is most clearly placed in time, usually a completed past event (`(document-creation-time :before e)`). Reputation or property states of that noun are `:contained` in the anchor, and the other events are `:overlap` under it.
  - `have-degree-91` gets no temporal parent and no modal parent. The event under its `:ARG2` does get them.

edits.old: - Every event has `:aspect`; negated events have `:polarity -`.
edits.new:
- Every event has `:aspect` (`have-degree-91` excepted); negated events have `:polarity -` (fused negation verbs excepted).
- Every Chinese predicate uses the sense and numbered roles of its own PropBank roleset.
- Before writing `:coref`, drop every pair where both mentions are only `:place`/`:mod` modifiers.
